worked_solution:
To determine whether the line $y=4x-5$ intersects the hyperbola $y=\frac{k+5}{x}+1$,  we need to solve the following system of equations for the two curves:      

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=4x-5 &  \\ y=\frac{k+5}{x}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and simplifying, we get a quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-5 & =\frac{k+5}{x}+1 \\ 4x-6 & =\frac{k+5}{x} \\ (4x-6)x & =k+5 \\ 4{x}^{2}-6x-k-5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the quadratic formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-(-6)\pm \sqrt{(-6)^{2}-4(4)(-k-5)}}{2(4)} \\  & =\frac{6\pm \sqrt{36+16k+80}}{8} \\  & =\frac{6\pm \sqrt{116+16k}}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

In order for the line to intersect the hyperbola only once, the quadratic formula above must give only one real solution.

So, the expression inside the square root must be equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}116+16k & =0 \\ 16k & =-116 \\ k & =-\frac{116}{16} \\ k & =-\frac{29\cdot 4}{4\cdot 4} \\ k & =-\frac{29}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the value of $k$ is $-\frac{29}{4}.$
